decisions.reason: ACE3 is the core of the firm's airfield lighting control business and was positioned as a new industry standard; it costs little to keep and will likely be developed further rather than abandoned.
The air situation display supports the tower and surveillance offer, which the MLAT launch reinforces; uncertainty remains but nothing points to failure, so the low-cost option stays open.
Training on airport systems is a cheap, recurring service that supports installed-base customers; airport activity recovering after the pandemic gives it renewed value.
The airfield ground lighting course ties directly to the firm's core lighting business and costs almost nothing to keep, so it remains a useful service option.

Collaboration software fits the strategy of integrated, collaborative decision-making; its value is still uncertain but promising, so the option is worth keeping open, though it may be rebranded or merged into a broader suite.

The MLAT system is a flagship that extends the firm toward integrated surveillance and automation; its strategic value is high and its uncertainty is not yet resolved, so management keeps investing in it.
